taxonomic_note: Accepted as Euphorbia villifera Scheele by current Kew/POWO and Flora of North America. Chamaesyce villifera is the principal legacy name in this project; Chamaesyce stanfieldii/Euphorbia stanfieldii are also treated as synonyms.
look_here_first: Do not use 'hairy' by itself. E. villifera is usually villous but can be glabrous. First look for the usually erect-to-ascending habit, then inspect the distinct filiform stipules and papillate leaf/stem surfaces. Confirm with the glabrous capsule: its cocci are often elongated and end in an empty distal portion.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew explicitly treats Chamaesyce villifera as a synonym of accepted Euphorbia villifera, native in Texas.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum sandmat: opposite leaves, milky latex, tiny cyathia, and 3-lobed capsules. In this trio, habit, stipule form, pubescence pattern, capsule structure, and seed surface are more reliable than the common name.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Annual or perennial herb with slender taproot or sometimes thickened woody rootstock; stems usually erect to ascending, rarely prostrate/decumbent, about 10–30 cm.
morphology_keys.stems: Papillate; usually villous but sometimes glabrous. Hair presence alone is therefore not absolute.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite; blades ovate, about 3–12 × 2–10 mm, base asymmetric and rounded to slightly cordate, margins entire or serrulate, surfaces usually villous but sometimes glabrous; leaf surfaces are papillate.
morphology_keys.stipules: Distinct, filiform, usually undivided, rarely split into 2–3 segments, about 0.3–0.7 mm; this differs strongly from the fused deltate stipule scale of E. serpens.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Cyathia solitary at distal nodes; 4 pink glands, oval/oblong/trapezoidal, with white-to-pink appendages.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsule oblate-deltoid, about 1.5–2 × 2.1–3.1 mm, glabrous; cocci are often elongated and terminate in an empty distal portion.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds gray-brown to red-brown, ovoid-oblong, weakly 4-angled, about 1–1.4 × 0.6–0.8 mm; smooth, faintly rugose, or with inconspicuous transverse ridges.
best_field_traits: usually erect to ascending rather than a flat rooted mat
usually villous foliage, but hairless forms occur
glabrous capsule with cocci often prolonged into an empty tip
weakly 4-angled seed, smooth to faintly rugose
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against E. serpens: villifera is usually erect/ascending, has distinct filiform stipules and papillate surfaces; serpens is a glabrous rooting mat with fused deltate stipules. Against E. prostrata: villifera has glabrous capsules and usually more generalized villous foliage; prostrata is more strictly prostrate and has crisped-villous capsule keels.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use the structural package, not the name: erect/ascending habit + filiform stipules + papillate surfaces + glabrous empty-tipped capsule cocci is much safer than 'hairy = villifera.'

unreliable_characters: hairiness by itself because glabrous forms occur
